title: Doenjang Jjigae
subtitle: Korean fermented soybean paste stew with tofu and vegetables
excerpt: Doenjang jjigae is a foundational Korean stew made with doenjang (fermented soybean paste), tofu, courgette, mushrooms, and onion in an anchovy or vegetable broth. It is deeply savoury and pungent with fermented complexity. Together with kimchi jjigae, it is the most representative of Korean everyday cooking.
sourceNotes: Doenjang (Korean fermented soybean paste) has been a cornerstone of Korean cooking for millennia, predating the introduction of chilli peppers. Doenjang jjigae appears at virtually every Korean meal alongside rice and banchan (side dishes). The paste is more pungent and earthy than Japanese miso; the stew is saltier and more intense than miso soup.

content.text: Doenjang jjigae is cooked on the hob in a clay pot (ttukbaegi) in Korea, which retains heat and keeps the stew bubbling at the table. A regular saucepan works fine. The stew should be served actively simmering in a bowl, with a bowl of plain rice alongside. The broth is salty and intense: this is intentional, and is balanced by the plain rice.
Pour 700 ml of water into a saucepan. Stir in the doenjang until dissolved. Bring to the boil over medium-high heat.
Add the onion, garlic, mushrooms, and courgette. Simmer for 8 minutes. Add the tofu cubes and gochugaru if using. Simmer for 5 more minutes. Do not stir vigorously or the tofu will break.
Taste the broth. It should be intensely savoury and salty. Adjust with a touch more doenjang if needed. Drizzle with sesame oil and scatter with spring onion. Serve in bowls with rice.

items.symptom: Stew lacks depth and tastes watery
items.cause: Not enough doenjang, or the paste was not fully dissolved
items.fix: Dissolve extra doenjang in a ladleful of the hot broth before adding back to the pot. Doenjang is the whole flavour base. Do not reduce it below 2 tablespoons per 700 ml of water.
